note: The City of Los Angeles' lot rules. Lot area and width by zone were read in the Los Angeles Municipal Code itself (Sections 12.05 to 12.12 and 17.05), in Internet Archive copies of the official code pages because the code's own site refuses automated reading: each source states its capture date, and a later amendment would not show. Zones ending in -H are the hillside lot-averaging minimums of Section 17.05 H, which the city may allow for part of a subdivision. Zones starting 1A: are Form Districts of the new zoning code (Chapter 1A), read on the city's own site; it applies only where the city has adopted it. The code prints no minimum lot depth. Chapter 1 measures lot width mid-lot and Chapter 1A on the street line; here width is what lies on the street line you name. Overlays and specific plans can change a figure. Not legal advice and not the city's form.

thresholds.what: In the City of Los Angeles the Parcel Map process creates at most this many lots.
thresholds.unit: lots

thresholds.note: City filing instructions, not the municipal code text (LAMC 13B.7.5 was not read).

thresholds.quote: The proposed subdivision and/or housing development project will result in 10 or fewer parcels/dwellings (not including a remainder parcel and Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU) or Junior ADUs if allowed).

thresholds.what: How Chapter 1 defines lot area.

thresholds.note: Read in an Internet Archive copy of the official code host page (the host itself answered HTTP 403); see the source edition for the capture date.

thresholds.what: How Chapter 1 measures lot width: between the side lot lines, at right angles to the depth, halfway between front and rear lot lines.

thresholds.what: How Chapter 1 defines lot depth (a definition only; no minimum depth is attached to it).
